- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early horizon.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.67), model underestimates; increase forecast lows, especially in late horizon.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00 followed by +0.67), leading to overcorrection; dampen immediate follow-up forecasts.
- Forecasts show strong mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is >10% above true, adjust downward by 10–20% in next 7d window.
- Sentiment volatility (alternating +/–) correlates with forecast instability; smooth forecasts when sentiment swings >0.50 in 3 consecutive days.
- Horizon-specific: 1–7d forecasts are often too aggressive; cap max deviation at 20% of recent 7d average.
- If true outcome exceeds 3x recent 18d mean, model overestimates; apply downward bias of 30–50% for 10d horizon.
- Sentiment +0.33/–0.33 transitions often trigger model lag; add 1–2d delay to forecast adjustment if sentiment shifts from neutral to strong.
